headline: Lionel Messi retires from Argentina's national team

sources.title: Argentina legend Lionel Messi announces international retirement
Lionel Messi announces retirement from Argentina national team
Jorge Messi, the father of Lionel, dies at 68

chunks.text: Lionel Messi has {{hung up}} his boots for Argentina's [[national team]]. He announced his [[retirement]] on Monday, August 31, after 20 years. He wrote the letter on July 21, two days after Argentina lost the World Cup [[final]] to Spain, 1-0 in [[extra time]]. He {{held off}} on publishing it because his father and [[longtime agent]], Jorge Messi, was [[seriously ill]]. His father {{passed away}} on August 8 at age 68, after a long [[illness]]. Messi said his father's death made him "even more [[convinced]]" the decision was right.

verbs.wrong: To score late in a game
verbs.why: A goalkeeper might hang up her gloves after 15 seasons, and a boxer can hang up his gloves after one last fight. Messi has hung up his boots for Argentina's national team after 20 years.

verbs.wrong: To keep a secret from family
verbs.why: Parents often hold off on buying a phone until a child is older, and a store can hold off on a sale until the weekend. Messi held off on publishing his letter because his father was seriously ill.

verbs.correct: To die, said in a gentle way
verbs.why: My grandmother passed away peacefully last spring, and the old family dog passed away at age 15. Messi's father passed away on August 8 at age 68, after a long illness.

chunks.text: Messi did not hide how hard the choice was. "It was a decision that hurt and hurts in a soul, but I understand that this is the moment," he wrote. He said he had "nothing left to give the national [[squad]]," and that a [[talented]] younger [[generation]] [[deserved]] the chance to play. For him, it is time to {{hand over}} the team and {{move on}}.

verbs.correct: To give control to another person
verbs.wrong: To ask for more time to decide
verbs.why: A retiring manager hands over the store to her deputy, and last year's winner hands over the trophy at the ceremony. Messi believes it is time to hand over the team to a talented younger generation.

verbs.correct: To accept a change and continue with life
verbs.wrong: To make a big decision in a hurry
verbs.why: After the shop closed, the owner moved on to a new business, and a family can move on after a hard year. Messi says he understands that this is the moment to move on.

chunks.text: When fans {{look back on}} his time with Argentina, the numbers tell the story. Messi {{racked up}} 207 [[appearances]] and 125 goals, and he retires as the country's [[all-time leader]] in both. He made his [[debut]] in 2005 and played in six World Cups. He won the 2021 Copa America, then {{went on}} to win the 2022 World Cup as [[captain]], ending Argentina's 36-year wait. He also won the 2024 Copa America.

verbs.correct: To think about a past time
verbs.wrong: To wait for a better chance
verbs.why: People look back on their school days with a smile, and a company looks back on its first year at a party. When fans look back on Messi's time with Argentina, the numbers alone tell the story.

verbs.correct: To collect a large total over time
verbs.wrong: To share credit with the whole team
verbs.why: A busy driver can rack up a lot of miles in a month, and a small mistake can rack up big bills. Messi racked up 207 appearances and 125 goals for Argentina.

verbs.correct: To continue and later achieve something
verbs.wrong: To leave a team before the season ends
verbs.why: She finished college and went on to become a doctor, and the small band went on to fill stadiums. Messi won the 2021 Copa America and then went on to win the 2022 World Cup as captain.

chunks.text: Even at his last [[tournament]], Messi {{stood out}}. Argentina {{fell short}} in the 2026 final, but he scored eight goals and finished second in the [[scoring race]]. The head of Argentina's soccer [[federation]] said it left the decision entirely up to Messi after the final. Argentina will now {{carry on}} without its captain, and the next generation has a big [[record]] to {{live up to}}.

verbs.correct: To be clearly better than the rest
verbs.wrong: To spend the game on the bench
verbs.why: A red coat stands out in a gray crowd, and one clear voice can stand out in a choir. Messi still stood out at his last tournament, with eight goals at the 2026 World Cup.

verbs.correct: To fail to reach a goal
verbs.wrong: To lose a player to injury
verbs.why: The team fell short of the playoffs by one point, and the charity fell short of its goal for the year. Argentina fell short in the 2026 final, losing 1-0 to Spain in extra time.
The store carried on after the owner retired, and the meeting carried on without the boss. Argentina will carry on without its captain.

verbs.correct: To be as good as something expected
verbs.wrong: To play for a team for many years
verbs.why: A new phone must live up to the ads, and a young singer tries to live up to her famous mother. The next generation of players has a very big record to live up to.

mainIdea.s: Argentina's all-time leading scorer has retired from the national team after the 2026 World Cup final. He delayed the news for weeks because his father was seriously ill and then died.
mainIdea.why: He wrote the letter on July 21, held off on publishing it while his father was ill, and announced the decision on August 31.

mainIdea.s: Argentina's captain retired from the national team because the federation decided it was time for younger players. He made the announcement the day after the World Cup final in July.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the federation left the decision entirely up to him, and the announcement came on August 31, weeks after the final.

mainIdea.s: Argentina's captain has signed a new deal to keep playing for the national team through the next Copa America. Team doctors cleared him after he missed most of the World Cup with an injury.
mainIdea.why: There is no new deal. He retired from the national team, and he played the whole World Cup, scoring eight goals.

lines.text: Did you see? Messi {{hung up}} his boots for the Argentina team. He announced it on Monday.
I saw. [[End of an era]]. Twenty years, six World Cups.
He wrote the letter back in July, right after the final against Spain. But he {{held off}} on publishing it.
Yes. His father was seriously ill, and he {{passed away}} on August 8. Messi said that made him even more convinced.
[[The timing says it all]]. He lost the final and his father in the same summer.
[[That's a lot for one summer]]. He said the decision hurt, but he understands this is the moment.
Still, what a record he leaves. 207 appearances, 125 goals.
He {{racked up}} more of both than anyone in Argentina's history. And after the 2021 Copa America, he {{went on}} to win the World Cup as captain.
[[You can't argue with those numbers]]. Even in his last tournament he {{stood out}}, didn't he?
Eight goals. Second in the scoring race, even though Argentina {{fell short}} in the final.
So what happens to the team now?
They {{carry on}} without him. He said a younger generation deserved the chance, and it's time to {{hand over}} the team and {{move on}}.
[[Big shoes to fill]]. That's a lot to {{live up to}}.
True. But when people {{look back on}} his career, they'll remember the trophies, not the goodbye.
